note: What each database actually holds for the parishes this archive needs. Checked before searching, every time — because a search of a source that does not cover your parish returns nothing, and nothing looks exactly like a negative result.

rows.note: Countess of Huntingdon's Chapel, Methodist Bishopston, Moravian Maudlin Street, Temple of Holy Cross. St Paul — the parish this archive needs — is not among them.
Stops 128 years before Hannah Saniger was born. Her baptism is untranscribed, not missing.
Covers the whole Saniger chain. This is where the chain was tested and failed.
With Dursley, holds 340 of the 494 Saniger records in the county.
Tested as the alternative reading of the tree's “Berkley”. The family there is SINGER throughout and holds no Hannah near 1805.

rows.holds: one D'Arcy record in the whole county
rows.note: That one record is Joseph D'Arcy's baptism, 19 March 1780, naming Robert and Jean. The 1779 marriage itself is not in the transcription.
Holds both the 1742 baptism that killed the Keele graft and the 1744 burial that may undo it.

128 Murdoch records exist for Ayrshire — Galston, Tarbolton, Ayr, Kirkoswald, Loudoun, Dailly, Beith, Dunlop — and not one for St Quivox. The county itself is thin: 202 Smiths for the whole eighteenth century.
Midlothian's holding is Edinburgh, Canongate, Restalrig and Dalry. Jean Ward's birth parish is not transcribed.
Zero records for the entire county. A control search for SMITH across the eighteenth century returns nothing. The county is offered in the search form and has no data behind it.
HO107/374 — this is where James and Hannah Wakefield were found, with Miriam aged one.

rows.holds: 221 Gloucestershire Wakefields, 31 in Bristol — but not this family
rows.note: Nationally only 36% of the 1851 pieces are transcribed. The piece covering Drivers Fields is not among them — which is why the Lyddya Sinegar identification is still an inference.
Control-tested at 21,248 Wakefield marriages for 1838–1842 before any absence was reported from it. This is where Miriam's birth registration was found.

rows.where: Prerogative Court of Canterbury wills, England
rows.holds: a wills index 1750–1800 and an administrations index 1660–1700
rows.note: NOTHING AFTER 1800. Three wills this archive needs — Robert D'Arcy's of 1827, Joseph D'Arcy's of 1848 and John Maddock Jones's of 1844 — are all beyond it. A paid trial does not help; the records are not there to unlock.

rows.where: Gloucestershire probate, Consistory Court of Gloucester
rows.note: Covers Berkeley and the whole Vale in the right years. Searched under wildcards for every form of the Saniger name and returns two entries, neither of them at Berkeley. A real negative, control-tested at 277 Smiths.

rows.where: Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage Licence Bonds, DUBLIN diocese
rows.note: Sorted by year, the latest Dublin-diocese entries in the entire set are a single 1813, a single 1752, and then a wall of 1741. The catalogue date range is the set's range, not the diocese's. An 1819 Wicklow marriage cannot be in it.

rows.where: Betham Prerogative Marriage Licences Abstracts, Ireland
rows.note: Ends nine years before the marriage this archive wants. Twenty-two Darcy entries, all necessarily too early.

rows.where: British consular and overseas registers (deaths abroad)
rows.note: Searched the whole record-set catalogue for “consular” and for “abroad” and both return no record sets at all. The Le Havre deaths of 1843 are not reachable here; they are on Ancestry and at Kew in RG 35.

rows.where: Caribbean Birth & Baptism Index — St Michael, Barbados
rows.note: Holds the two christenings of Robert D'Arcy's children at St Michael in 1786 and 1788. Barbados Births & Baptisms 1637-1891, a separate and larger set, holds neither — two indexes of the same island disagreeing about what is in them, which is its own warning.

The index is searchable on a paid trial and the transcripts are not — “Subscribe to unlock exclusive records”. Joseph D'Arcy's whole artillery career and a Constantine D'Arcy entry of 1777-79 are visible as dates and unreadable as records.

rows.where: any census set, when a YEAR OF BIRTH and a PLACE are combined
rows.note: A query carrying both yearofbirth and keywordsplace returns ZERO on census sets and presents it as a clean negative. Control: JANE SMITH born about 1788 in Sussex, 1871 — zero. The same search returns 60 by year alone and 136 by place alone. Search on one or the other and filter by hand.

rows.where: a NAMED CEMETERY — Centenary Memorial Gardens, Brisbane
rows.note: Searching inside a named cemetery works and produced three D'Arcy memorials with plots and dates. This archive had never used the source.

rows.where: by SURNAME AND STATE — location=Queensland, locationId=state_2118
rows.note: Returns NO MATCHES for D'Arcy, Darcy, Sneyd — and for SMITH, which is impossible, while Darcy worldwide returns 10,654. The locationId is wrong. Search within a cemetery instead.

The site loads and its own search API then answers 403 and 400; the country list never finishes loading and the page sits on “Please wait”. Nothing was searched, so nothing is known — this is a blocked source and not an empty one.

rows.where: ARIENZO, Caserta — the parish this family married into
rows.holds: 422 REGISTERS: Matrimoni processetti 63, Matrimoni 62, Nati 59, Morti 57, Diversi 45, and more
rows.note: Digitised in full and free to read — AND NOT NAME-INDEXED. A search for FALCO at Arienzo returns nothing, and so does a search for RUSSO, the commonest surname in Campania, which is the control that proves the index rather than the family is missing. Antenati says so itself: only part of its registers are indexed. These 422 must be read page by page. The marriage PROCESSETTI are the prize, because they carry birth extracts and parental consents for both parties.

rows.db: National Library of Ireland parish registers
rows.where: the Limerick line — Atkinson, Cole, Creech, Kent, Bowen, Peevers
rows.note: The NLI collection is Catholic by definition, and this line is not. Paul Cole Atkinson is recorded as born at ST MARY'S, LIMERICK — the Church of Ireland cathedral parish — and the surnames around him are Protestant settler names. The same shape as the Wicklow problem: the right records are the ones the NLI does not hold.

rows.where: the Creech, Atkinson and Mulcahy lines
rows.note: A Cloudflare bot check, for the third time in this archive's life. Not defeated, and will not be. The free official Irish index remains unreachable from here and stays on the errand list for a person with a browser.
Reachable, and behind Login / Register / Subscribe. Limerick and both Tipperarys are among its counties. It is a subscription, so it is an errand and not a search.

The old-parish-register search area answers ACCESS DENIED without an account. No account was created and no credentials were entered. Jean Ward's 1754 baptism and her parents' 1747 marriage are already held here from FamilySearch; what ScotlandsPeople would add is the register image itself.

The search page opens with no login and accepts a POST, and then returns the results-page furniture with NO RESULT ROWS for every query. Control: SMITH BIRTHS IN BRISTOL IN 1840 returns zero, which is impossible, and so does Wakefield — a birth this archive already holds from the GRO index at vol 11 p.183. Nothing was searched. Every zero taken from it here is meaningless.

rows.where: the Hornby claim and the Keele graft
rows.note: “You are not allowed to search for posts in this forum. Please login below or register.” Searching needs an account, let alone posting. No account was created. Putting the Hornby evidence to the forum is a job for a person with a login, and is now an errand.

rows.holds: 26 records in Italy, Marriages 1809-1900, with both spouses named
rows.note: Readable WITHOUT signing in, and no bot check appeared. Falco brides and grooms at Arienzo with their spouses — Loffredo, Abatiello, Di Lucia, Librera, Perrotta — and FALCO GIOVANNA married to CRISCI ANIELLO, Crisci being one of the Falco archive's own surnames. This is that archive's ground; the coverage is recorded here, not the records.

The category filter mangles to `life-events-bmds` in the URL and the search then returns zero whatever else is asked, while the same query without it returns results. The third broken FindMyPast parameter found in two days, after yearofbirth+keywordsplace on the census and the Find a Grave locationId.

rows.where: the whole of Gloucestershire, by hundred, manor and tithing
rows.holds: nearly every man aged 16–60 in the county, with trade, age-decade and stature
rows.note: Searched 14 September 2026 for all seventeen spellings this archive held, then exhaustively by word-ending (-gar, -gear, -ger, -gor, -gre). Eleven men of the surname, in four spellings, two of them new. Control: 676 men returned for Dursley, 42 for Halmore.

rows.where: any surname search ending in an asterisk
rows.note: A wildcard at the END of a term silently matches nothing: `Sanige*` returns no matches while `Saniger` returns five. A wildcard at the START works — `*niger` returns seven. The fourth broken search parameter this archive has caught by control test, after two on FindMyPast and Find a Grave's locationId.

rows.where: any search returning exactly one record
rows.holds: the record — but not in digits
rows.note: A single hit is reported as “There is one match”, spelling the number as a word; two or more are reported in digits. A reader or script looking for a numeral sees nothing and files a zero. This hid JOHN SANIGER — the one man living inside the hamlet the surname comes from — on the first pass of the search that found him, and he was recovered only because a search by PLACE returned him and contradicted the null.

rows.where: Berkeley, Dursley, Wotton-under-Edge and Uley registration districts
rows.holds: the registrars' own books, indexed to register and entry number
rows.note: Free, and it gives the LOCAL reference a certificate is ordered against, which the GRO index does not. Its surname box does prefix matching when Exact Match is unticked, so the stem SANIG finds every form at once — searched as SANIGER alone it misses Lydia Sanigar entirely.

rows.holds: a great deal, and not the piece this archive needs
rows.note: SMITH returns the 1,000-row display cap for 1851, 1861 and 1871, which looks like full coverage and is not. The three D'Arcy sisters are enumerated in the 1851 Sussex census under the surname ARCY at HO107/1646 folio 357 — and FreeCEN returns nought for Arcy in Sussex in 1851. Test a free census index with a record you already know is in it, never with a common surname.

rows.where: any search returning a large number
rows.holds: up to 500 rows, and says so
rows.note: FreeREG stops counting at 500. Any control reported as “more than 500” is a ceiling, not a measurement: it reads identically whether a county is half transcribed or whole. Two nulls in this archive were justified that way and have been re-controlled — at PARISH level, with a surname whose count comes in UNDER the cap. Ruabon returns 500 Joneses and 39 Smiths for 1780–1830; the 39 is the number that means something. (Recorded as UNUSABLE: it is unusable specifically as a control.)

rows.where: Every repository in England, not only Kew
rows.holds: a great deal, and it is free to search without any account
rows.note: Searching Discovery needs no sign-in; only downloading images does. Under the MEDIEVAL spellings it returns 195 records for this surname against 71 for the modern one — 178 of them at Berkeley Castle, and the rest at Gloucestershire, Kew, Birmingham, Bristol, Hertford and Aberystwyth. Tested 15 September 2026.

rows.holds: the deeds themselves, calendared item by item — party, land, rent, witnesses, and the GC number to quote when ordering
rows.note: The modern catalogue this archive had been asking for as errand 51 turns out to be free and already open. 178 records under the medieval spellings.

rows.holds: a thirty-year fragment and nothing else
rows.note: Controlled at PARISH level on 15 September with SMITH: 3 exact and 36 uncertain results, every one between 1653 and 1677. County-level queries here are meaningless — FreeREG caps at 500, so a common surname returns the cap whether a parish is fully transcribed or absent.

FreeREG has data for 189 Gloucestershire places, including Berkeley, Dursley, North Nibley, Slimbridge, Thornbury, Uley and Woodmancote. NEITHER AWRE NOR BLAKENEY IS ONE OF THEM. Any Awre search would have returned nothing for a reason that has nothing to do with the family. **AND THE PREMISE WAS WRONG:** this archive has no Sanigers at Awre or Blakeney at all — correction 32. The absence of coverage there is real and irrelevant.

rows.where: England and Wales, the GRO index
rows.holds: the registrations, and it will lie to you about a wide date range
rows.span: 1837 onwards, 99%+ for the quarters that matter here
rows.note: IT SILENTLY REFUSES a range of more than a few years and redisplays its own search form, which is indistinguishable from an empty result. Three searches were recorded as nought on 15 September before a control — Charlotte Darcy, 1869, Brighton 2b 152 — showed they had never run. Narrowed to three years it works perfectly.

rows.holds: commissions and promotions — but not Ordnance ones before the American war
rows.note: Free, no account, richly digitised — 1,057 notices mention «Lieutenant» in the 1770s alone. But notices mentioning «Corps of Engineers» number NONE in 1774, NONE in 1775, and three in 1776 of which one is Irish and two are a Bengal reprint. The Ordnance began gazetting engineer commissions during the American war. A silence here about 1776 is about the Gazette, not about the man.

rows.holds: nearly every adult male in England, for the counties that survive
rows.note: For Gloucestershire, nothing. The series is one alphabetical run of county bundles and GLOUCESTERSHIRE IS MISSING FROM WHERE IT BELONGS — the piece that would hold it holds Essex, Hampshire, Hertfordshire and Huntingdonshire instead. The alphabet is the control. Staffordshire, for the Sneyds, does survive.

rows.where: Gloucestershire Archives D 1874/1, photostats of the surviving originals
rows.holds: named adults, for the hundreds whose membranes survive
rows.note: The catalogue lists every surviving membrane: Salmonsbury, Holford and Greston, Kiftsgate, Tibblestone, Rapsgate, Bradley, Crowthorne, Brightwells Barrow, Longtree, Cirencester, Bisley, St Briavels. BERKELEY HUNDRED IS NOT AMONG THEM. What survives is Cotswold and Forest; the Vale is lost.

rows.db: Rudder, A New History of Gloucestershire (1779)
rows.holds: the tithings, hamlet by hamlet — but not this hamlet
rows.note: 5.7 million characters, Berkeley mentioned 804 times, and NOT ONE mention of Saniger under any spelling. The control holds: his index carries «Wanfwell in Berkeley 280», Hamfallow, Halmore and Alkington. At page 280 the whole tithing is «Hamfallow, in which are Wanſwell… part of Halmore; and Hamfallow». Smyth names the hamlet in 1639 and Bigland in 1791; Rudder, between them, does not.

rows.holds: reviews of the editions this archive relies on
rows.note: One hit in four volumes read, and it corrects this archive: reviewing Maclean's 1902 edition of the 1608 muster it says «Sainger should read Saniger». Three further volumes are a clean null against a Berkeley control of 234, 91 and 51 mentions. Too small a family for an antiquarian serial — but the right place to check an edition.

rows.db: The manorial court rolls of Awre
rows.where: Gloucestershire Archives — D2156/1–4, D421/M7, D3270/362, D3270/363
rows.holds: tenants by name, generation after generation, with the customary heir of each who died
rows.note: Not digitised; the catalogue is free and the documents are a visit. **They are also not about this family.** This row was added on the strength of an invented «Forest side» — correction 32 — and is kept, corrected, because the rolls are genuinely a model of what a surviving manorial run looks like.

rows.holds: named taxpayers, hundred by hundred, in the century this archive cannot otherwise cross
rows.note: Catalogued individually and described as «Assessment (individuals)», so the names are known to be there. NOT DIGITISED and no free published edition exists. For BLEDISLOE — Awre and Blakeney — this matters more than anywhere else: that hundred has no FreeREG coverage, no surviving Protestation return and no surviving 1381 poll tax membrane.

rows.db: The Gentleman's Magazine, on the Internet Archive
rows.holds: officers' deaths and obituaries — for the years it happens to hold
rows.note: The search index stamps EVERY volume «1731», the series start, so year-targeted retrieval needs the per-item metadata record fetched one at a time. Checked that way on 15 September: the 120 volumes include 1827, 1829, 1847 and **1849** — and **neither 1805 nor 1848**, which are the years Constantine and Joseph D'Arcy died. The 1849 volume was read: 122 obituary sections, three D'Arcys, none of them this family's.

rows.span: to about 1790, and then effectively nothing
rows.note: Measured on 16 September by asking for **every burial at Berkeley, any surname**, in two equal thirty-year windows. **1735-1765 returns 442. 1800-1830 returns 2.** The surname series behaves the same way: 23 SANIGER burials at Berkeley, the last of them in **1787**. Any «not buried at Berkeley» this archive states from this set after about 1790 is a statement about the index and not about the churchyard — including John Saniger, whose burial there in January 1825 is documented from elsewhere and is **not** in this set.

**272 marriages at Berkeley for 1793-1803**, any surname. That is what makes the absence of a Saniger marriage there in that decade — under eight spellings — a real null rather than a gap, and it is why the tree's «John Saniger married Lydia Jones at Berkeley in 1797» could be disproved rather than merely doubted. The result rows do **not** show the spouse's surname; the transcript does.

rows.holds: parish baptisms, with the father's first name
rows.note: 158 SANIGER entries read in full, 115 of them Berkeley, 156 of the 158 naming a father. The apparent hole at Berkeley from **1632 to 1676 is a spelling and not a gap** — SAINGER supplies 26 entries inside it. About one entry in five is a duplicate: 125 distinct name-year-place combinations in 158 rows.

rows.where: every repository Discovery indexes, not Kew alone
rows.note: `GET /API/search/records?sps.searchQuery=…` returns JSON with a count and a paged records array, and needs **no account, no key and no bot check** — which is the whole difference between a question and a measurement. Wrapped as `tools/discovery.py` on 17 September and control-tested against nonsense terms before its counts were used. It returns the CATALOGUE, not the documents: every description is a modern cataloguer's reading, and two of the best ones here carry the cataloguer's own «[Saniger?]» in brackets.

Measured on 21 September by asking the same question of two counties. **SMITH returns 3 baptisms in Hampshire and 41,098 in Kent.** The set is a FamilySearch transcription and Hampshire is simply not in it. This archive has never built a Hampshire finding on it — Joseph D'Arcy's baptism, his siblings and his parents' marriage all come from the **Hampshire Genealogical Society's own county sets**, which are separate record sets on the same site. Recorded so that nobody reaches for the national set and reports Portsea empty.

Measured on 21 September, one surname, one query shape, one session. **SMITH returns 0 marriages in Hampshire across the whole 435-year span and 14,056 in Gloucestershire.** Not few — none. Nothing about a search box produces that: the same page, the same afternoon, returns fourteen thousand for the county next door. **This voids every Hampshire marriage null this archive has recorded against the national set**, including «no Joseph D'Arcy marries in Hampshire between 1825 and 1835», which was a statement about the transcription and not about Joseph. The county sets on the same site are unaffected.

rows.holds: twenty-three entries, and some of them are not Hampshire
rows.note: The third of the three FamilySearch national sets, asked the same way on 21 September: **SMITH returns 23 in Hampshire and 4,600 in Gloucestershire.** And the 23 do not survive reading — the first two are at **Easton-Maudit** and **Paulersbury**, which are Northamptonshire villages filed under the wrong county. All three national sets are therefore unusable for Hampshire, and a Hampshire question must go to the Hampshire Genealogical Society's county sets or to civil registration.

rows.holds: the GRO death index, addressable by district
rows.note: **21 PITT deaths registered at Lymington between 1820 and 1900**, and **two D'Arcy deaths in the whole run of the index** — Joseph in the first quarter of 1848 and Katherine Lucy Elizabeth in the second of 1863, both of whom this archive already holds. The district is plainly indexed, so the absence of any other D'Arcy there is a fact about the family and not about the set.

rows.db: FindMyPast — England & Wales Non-Conformist Births and Baptisms (RG 4)
rows.holds: the Bristol chapel registers, indexed and searchable by place
rows.note: **SMITH returns 133 chapel baptisms at Bristol**, Congregational and Presbyterian. The series this archive spent a week planning to order volume by volume from The National Archives is transcribed here and answerable in one query. **`S*N*G*R` at Bristol returns nought**, against 808 for the same wildcard nationally and 8 for SANIGAR — all eight at Dursley, Corn Meeting. The set also feeds England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975, so that set is not purely Anglican.

`S*N*G*R` at Bristol returns **nine** — Singer, Springer, Stringer, Swearenger — and none of them is this surname. **409 under the same wildcard across the whole set.** A null against a query that returns nine near misses at the right place is a null worth having.

rows.db: FindMyPast — every Birth, Marriage, Death & Parish record set
rows.holds: the British armed forces overseas registers, and nothing earlier
rows.note: Asked across the whole category on 21 September rather than set by set. **D'ARCY at Barbados returns four records, all between 1850 and 1876**, every one of them from *British Armed Forces And Overseas Births And Baptisms* or the matching deaths set. **Control: SMITH at Barbados returns eight, and the oldest is 1811** — a Royal Regiment of Foot deaths register. There is nothing here from the eighteenth century at all. **Constantine's christening at St Michael in February 1786 and Jane's in March 1788 are not on this site and cannot be**, which settles how errand 33 has to be answered: from the Barbados originals or a repository copy, not from another index search.

rows.holds: a name index to BMD notices, weighted to the twentieth century
rows.note: **It is not the British Newspaper Archive.** It indexes birth, marriage and death notices by name; the Year and Location columns are empty for most rows, so **any year filter silently returns zero** — SMITH gives 674,001 unfiltered and 0 for 1827 ± 2. Read whole rather than filtered, **Robert D'Arcy returns 42 notices with nothing dated before 1857 and Joseph D'Arcy 84 with nothing before 1914.** Useful for the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries; useless for this archive's Georgian questions, which need the full-text site and its own sign-in.

rows.db: English marriage registers, 1754–1837 (the record class itself)
rows.where: every English parish, Hardwicke's Act to civil registration
rows.holds: the two names, the parish, banns or licence, the signatures and the witnesses — and NOTHING ELSE
rows.note:
**No fathers, abodes, ages, conditions or occupations.** Bristol Archives stated it in those words on 22 September, reading the 1828 entry this archive had waited nine days for. Fathers arrive with civil registration in **1837**, which is why the 1871 marriage in this family names one and the 1828 marriage cannot. This row exists because three errands here were written on the opposite assumption. **Before asking a marriage entry for a father, check its date.**

**One qualifier, so this row does not create the opposite error.** A father can still appear on a pre-1837 entry incidentally — most often as consent for a party under twenty-one — and banns books sometimes carry more than the register does. What does not exist before 1837 is a **father's column**. And consent was recorded for marriages **by licence**: under Hardwicke's Act a marriage **by banns** stood unless a parent publicly dissented while they were read, so nothing was written down. **Thomas and Martha married by banns**, which is the one detail that decides it.

rows.where: Bristol Church of England parishes, including St James
rows.holds: the original registers, read by staff on request
rows.note: Answered a seven-part enquiry in nine days, **free**, having viewed the record — their research service is quoted at £13 for up to half an hour and nothing was charged. The reply corrected this archive's spelling of the surname from the index reading and volunteered a record nobody had asked for. Images of the registers are on **Ancestry**, which this archive will not use because it wants an account.

good: the source holds this class of record for this place and period
partial: it covers some of it — a window, a parish, a subset
absent: examined, and it does not hold this at all
unusable: it exists but cannot settle the question — a cap, a fragment, an index that lies about its own emptiness
blocked: reachable only behind an account or a bot check this archive will not pass. NOT the same as «cannot answer»: nobody has asked it
